event.summary: Retired-session dead tabs deliberately remain for Delete
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.
TLDR: Dead shell tabs in retired containerized sessions remain until the user deletes the session.
Details: The two automatic reapers now skip a session whose stored launch is retired before spending admission budget (ticker.rs:2095 and :2167). Considered whether that leaves cleanup indefinitely pending. SPEC.md, Retired containerized sessions, lines 4818-4821 explicitly states: ‘Existing sessions support Delete only. Opening terminals or tabs, exec, Stop, Restart, Clone, Replace and Replace with are refused. Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence.’ Leaving these tabs for whole-session Delete is consistent with that restriction and avoids repeatedly admitting refused closes. The added test asserts no lifecycle claims on retired sessions and full admission budget for ordinary sessions. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from retaining already-dead tabs. Confidence: confirmed from source and contract, not execution. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance quoted above. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: whole-session Delete implementation is an interface owned outside this patch group; no independent audit of that implementation is claimed.

event.summary: Host-tab test may inspect cleanup before close tasks complete
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.
TLDR: The new regression test may fail depending on whether asynchronous tab cleanup has finished.
Details: The test releases four held close tasks, then calls wait_for_reaped_panes with an empty slice for its host-tab branch before asserting all ordinary host-tab cells are empty. Need to inspect that helper and the close-task completion boundary to determine whether this establishes readiness or merely yields incidentally. The helper was located at ticker.rs:2692 but has not yet been read. Suggested bucket: other (test reliability); could-be-highest: no. Confidence: uninvestigated lead; no execution performed. proposed_drop: false pending source checks. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Missing premise: whether wait_for_reaped_panes with zero panes waits for lifecycle claims or host-tab cell removal. Next check: helper and owned tab-close source at the same revision.

event.summary: Host-tab test waits for all lifecycle claims before asserting cleanup
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.
TLDR: The suspected race in the new cleanup test is ruled out by its completion helper.
Details: Original suspected consequence was a test failure from inspecting host-tab cleanup before its four close tasks completed. Source check: wait_for_reaped_panes at ticker.rs:2692-2720 requires both no named panes AND no lifecycle claim for any session in the fixture, even with an empty pane slice. The helper's declared contract says the close holds that claim through teardown. The added test also checks every ordinary session is claimed before releasing the gate (:3242-3264), so the wait cannot mistake unstarted tasks for completed ones. No execution performed. Suggested bucket: other (test reliability); could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: source refutation, the helper waits for owned close completion rather than just pane absence. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this conclusion depends on the lifecycle claim spanning close teardown as documented; the owned-close caller will also be inspected to validate that contract.

event.summary: Terminal-kind report removal is fenced by a protocol bump
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e.
TLDR: Removing the old/new-terminal details does not silently connect incompatible old and new peers.
Details: Considered whether deleting report_new_terminals and entry_info's agent_terminal projection could leave an older client believing these sessions still need migration, or choose an unsupported stream. Source check: the same commit's crates/farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs changes PROTOCOL_VERSION from 76 to 77 and removes both SessionInfo fields, along with the raw stream variants. The listing and single-session boundary no longer need to add a field absent from the new wire contract. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed from source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, explicit incompatible-protocol fence accompanies the report removal. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this is a review of these status projections and their protocol interface, not an independent review of all grid-stream removal changes.

event.summary: Old-terminal-ended notices are not erased by warning resolution
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4; removal follow-up 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333.
TLDR: The new notice explaining why an old agent stopped survives later startup and conversation recovery.
Details: Checked whether adding OldTerminalEnded to NotificationKind::ALL could cause the generic resume resolver or startup's old-warning resolver to erase it. Both resolves_on_resume and requires_no_identity match it explicitly as false (notifications.rs:143 and :162), and its stored key is distinct old_terminal_ended (:179). core/old_terminals.rs:525-550 writes the notice at the converted generation, then resolves only old_terminal. It writes before publication and reload loads the history. The follow-up deletes the obsolete ticker warning producer, not this startup writer. SPEC.md, Status, at 1ed482d lines 2810-2817 says the new notice stays unresolved across later starts. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence from the suspected notice-resolution defect. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation, both resolution paths distinguish the new kind. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveats: best-effort persistence can omit a notice after a write failure, but this is the documented diagnostic contract, not introduced by the new enum routing.

event.summary: Gone-host report documentation contradicts the anchor contract
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333.
TLDR: The new source documentation incorrectly promises that a waiting conversation report is discarded when its terminal host is gone. The implementation can keep retrying it, or still accept it from retained process evidence.
Details: report_files.rs:43-55 newly replaces the tmux-specific explanation with claims that a gone terminal host is definitive and a report whose terminal is gone is discarded. Actual source: core.rs:15826-15853 host_agent_anchor returns Internal if the same-generation published entry has no terminal, or host.anchor() returns None. report_files.rs:252-261 treats Internal as Retry. hosts/terminal.rs:872-883 explicitly permits Liveness::Gone to yield a TerminalAnchor when child_pid > 1, so even a gone handle need not reject a report: retained child evidence can still anchor it. Thus neither the definitive discard claim nor the implied requirement that the host still hold the terminal is accurate. Suggested fix: document retained child anchors and retry behavior accurately; if definitive rejection is intended, specify and implement that separately rather than teaching a contract the code does not enforce. Suggested bucket: other (documentation/contract correctness). could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; retained anchors carry start identity and the per-generation fence remains. Confidence: confirmed through source and caller analysis; no execution or reproductions performed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Material caveat: the underlying host retry/retained-anchor behavior already exists in the parent revision (core.rs:17044-17066); this finding concerns the inaccurate replacement documentation introduced by this patch, not a newly introduced runtime regression. The original suspected consequence of retrying indefinitely after permanent host loss is supported by the None-terminal/Internal/Retry path, but is pre-existing and is not independently charged to this change.

event.summary: Held Restart rows retain coherent listing and terminal-report boundaries
event.detail:
Reviewed commits: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513 and f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e.
TLDR: The report/listing cleanup does not cause a restarting session to disappear or expose an entry-local false terminal report.
Details: Discovery pass 1 traced the held-row fallback because it can originate from entry.info, whose supervisor_creates_host_terminals field starts false. At 647f0227 listing.rs applies report_new_terminals to every projected row, held ones included, after joining the map and held snapshots. The fallback is therefore overwritten to true at the actual reply boundary. core.rs:13286-13317 swaps the held row/tab cell and removes the entry while holding sessions; :13762-13803 republishes and removes held state under that same lock. listing.rs reads both under sessions and filters duplicate IDs. Later f560058d removes the report only when its wire field itself is removed; the held/live join and lock remain intact at listing.rs:111-145. A retained pre-Restart status is intentional rather than a fresh exit observation during replacement. Suggested bucket: other if broken; could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no runtime execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, shared reply boundary overwrites held defaults before the field is retired, and coordinated locking preserves one row. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage search. Caveat: this checks the assigned listing changes and immediate publication interface, not the correctness of all Restart mutation paths. No unresolved premise remains.
